findings.text: blocking: the new None branch at imas_codex/standard_names/review/pipeline.py:1993 cannot fire on the reviewed production path, because imas_codex/standard_names/review/pipeline.py:594 sets batch['error_lint_findings'] = {} when state.audit_report is None (cli/sn.py:6565 skips Layer 1 for --skip-audit) and imas_codex/standard_names/review/pipeline.py:1136 then passes batch.get('error_lint_findings', {}) rather than the None the docstring reserves for 'the checks did not run'. A `sn review --skip-audit --target docs` pass therefore reaches the cap with {}, treats it as a run that found nothing, and calls clear_holds_not_raised for every scored entry, clearing each docs_lint_error hold and releasing the document through _promote_if_eligible with the lint check never having run. That is the mirror of the defect the reconciliation was added to fix, and the guard the node wrote for it (test_a_lint_hold_is_not_cleared_when_the_checks_did_not_run) exercises the None the production callers never send. The distinction has to hold on the path that actually runs: either the enrich pass must leave the key absent when state.audit_report is None and the call sites must pass None through, or the cap needs a separate 'checks ran' flag.

non-blocking: this covering test for _cap_docs_scores_for_lint_errors was run by no gate arm. It calls the cap with the batch's empty mapping and no graph= and no stub, so the reconciliation added by a645d8b3b now drives clear_holds_not_raised -> GraphClient against the live database from a test that carries no graph marker and needed no graph at base. The same hazard was recognised and stubbed for tests/standard_names/test_review_findings_cap.py at 50bd96ef3; this third caller was missed, so the named gate is a subset of the files the brief asks it to cover.

non-blocking: test_dismissal_does_not_accept_a_quarantined_document does not isolate the quarantine exclusion it is named for. Its planted row carries no HAS_REVIEW edge, so PROMOTE_STRANDED_DOCS_WHERE (graph_ops.py:12558) refuses it on docs_review_eligibility_where() alone; deleting the coalesce(validation_status,'') <> 'quarantined' clause leaves this test green, so the quarantine half of the gate the node adopted here is taken on the owner's word rather than measured by this change. Carried unchanged from the prior review of this node.

non-blocking: the reconciliation-controls bullet states 'Removing the clearing call from the cascade route reddens the cascade release test', but the logged control (negative-control-reconcile.log, control 1) reverted the whole answering commit, so the test reddens with AttributeError: module 'imas_codex.standard_names.review.cascade' has no attribute 'sync_route_holds' rather than on the clearing direction. The cascade release test does guard the direction by its own assertion - the logged control simply does not show it - and the same bullet's sibling claim for the lint cap (control 2, an assertion failure) is correct. The same fragment, at line 187, states the head arm as '93 passed' where gate-head.log ends '9 failed, 96 passed, 1 skipped'.

non-blocking: after_suite records 'Head arm at 50bd96ef3 over the same four files: 9 failed, 96 passed, 1 skipped', but the log it names, gate-head.log, carries '# revision: 468ceb18007dde1627c5bb66d738e09367f8a014' on its second line - the commit before the last. The counts are identical, and the intervening commit 50bd96ef3 only stubs a writer in a test file, so the delta is materially unaffected; the receipt nevertheless names a revision no logged arm was run at, which is the fact a promotion record is read for.

non-blocking: baseline_suite records '9 failed, 79 passed, 1 skipped' for the base arm, but gate-base.log ends '9 failed, 79 passed, 1 skipped, 1 warning, 10 errors in 28.34s' - ten fixture setup errors from tests/standard_names/test_review_holds.py (FileNotFoundError on a deleted basetemp at /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/.../bt/review-holds-62kffnmy), i.e. the base arm did not actually measure that file in the four-file configuration. The manifest does state the separate base run of that file (10 passed, gate-base-holds.log). Since the ten error at base and pass at head the omission flatters the head arm rather than the reverse, and the nine shared failing ids are unaffected.
